title: Same gap, a visible reason
hook: Does a pay difference feel different when productivity differences are visible?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare unequal pay with and without observable performance justification.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare unequal pay with and without observable performance justification.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy worker earns €100 for ten units and a peer €150 for fifteen. What is the gap in pay per produced unit? Toy inputs A=[100, 10, 150, 15]; B=[100, 10, 150, 10].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[10, 10, 0], [10, 15, 5]]. Labels: A €/unit, B €/unit, Gap €/unit.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Unequal total pay can coexist with equal pay per output unit. The comparison holds output equal instead. A fairness interpretation therefore depends on which relevant difference is visible, not the pay gap alone.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses A pay €=100, A units=10, B pay €=150, B units=10. What is Gap €/unit? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses A pay €=100, A units=10, B pay €=150, B units=10. What is Gap €/unit?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Indian workers paid less than peers cut output and attendance, unless the pay gap matched visible productivity differences (Breza, Kaur & Shamdasani, 2018).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare unequal pay with and without observable performance justification.
